next.reason: Part 1, a space may follow any separator: §2023:8.3.5 SR9 keeps it 'except the opening delimiter of a literal' (1985: opening quotation mark). Part 2, punctuation inside a PICTURE character-string or numeric literal is a symbol, not a separator: §2023:8.3.5 SR2 and SR3 make comma, semicolon and period separators only when a space follows, and §2023:8.3.5 SR4 exempts parentheses 'Except when appearing in a picture character-string'. So pictures and numeric literals still end only at space, comma, semicolon or period. Part 3, separator rules do not apply inside literals: the uncataloged §2023:8.3.5 preamble says 'A separator is one of the following, except when appearing in a literal'. 2023 has no comment-entries, and comment lines (§2023:6.3.7.2, uncataloged) are not character-strings. The removal of comment-entries belongs to the paragraph rules that carried them. Catalog defect: the 8.3.5 preamble has no rule id.
